body.statement: For every sequence of nonempty shells on which the legal same-shell deformation property posed in Open-ended Question 2 holds with constants uniform in \(N\) and \(s_N\), \(c\min\{1,(Ns_N^2)^{-1}\}\le\inf_{\widetilde\mu}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}\mathbb E_P L(\widetilde\mu,\mu(P))\le C_0\min\{1,(Ns_N^2)^{-1}\}\). The lower inequality ranges over every measurable estimator of the entire observed sample. For every nonempty shell, without the deformation premise, only the upper inequality is asserted and is attained by \(\widehat\mu\).
body.justification: Conditional on the visible legal-deformation obligation, the matched frontier turns the APM eigenvalue into the exact information scale; achievability remains unconditional on nonempty shells.
body.gap: Lei and Ross require the APM gap to dominate estimation noise, and Yan and Wainwright study a different growing-matrix experiment; conditional on legal same-shell pairs, this theorem supplies the missing fixed-panel complete-law converse against the same observable-shell upper bound.
body.consumer: Researchers using \(\operatorname{apm}\) or \(\operatorname{fect}\) obtain a necessary and sufficient signal-to-sample-size condition for reliable counterfactual recovery.
body.proof_tex:
The unconditional upper inequality is exactly \(\operatorname{lem:pca-upper}\). For the lower inequality, apply \(\operatorname{lem:two-point-decision-lower-bounds}\) to the two laws in the displayed premise with \(\kappa=1/8\) and \(\Delta\geq c_0r_N\). Since \(\sqrt{\kappa/2}=1/4\), every estimator satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}\mathbb E_PL(\widetilde\mu,\mu(P))
\geq\frac38\min\{1,c_0^2r_N^2/4\}
\geq c r_N^2.
\]
Because \(r_N^2=\min\{1,(Ns_N^2)^{-1}\}\), taking the infimum over all measurable estimators proves the result.
